objectives: This course aims to support PhD students in the systematic development and progress of their doctoral dissertations through regular academic discussion with their advisors. Students will refine their research questions, theoretical foundations, research design, methodology, data analysis, and interpretation of findings under faculty guidance.
content:
The course is conducted primarily through regular dissertation discussions between PhD students and their advisors. Course activities will be tailored to each student’s stage of dissertation development and may include discussion of research topics, research questions, literature review, theoretical framework, hypothesis or proposition development, research design, data collection, analytical methods, interpretation of results, academic writing, and preparation for dissertation proposal or defense.

Students will periodically present their research progress, receive feedback from their advisors, revise their work accordingly, and address theoretical, methodological, and practical issues that arise during the research process. The course emphasizes continuous research development, academic rigor, and timely progress toward completion of the doctoral dissertation.
